rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: England uses three Environment Agency warning types: flood alert, flood warning and severe flood warning.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: A flood alert means flooding is possible and people should prepare.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: A flood warning means flooding is expected and people should act.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: A severe flood warning means flooding could endanger life and significantly disrupt communities.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Severe flood warnings can be issued before, during or after flooding where life and communities are threatened.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood alerts may be issued when river forecasts indicate flooding is possible.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood alerts may cover high tides, surges or strong winds at sea.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood warnings may cover heavy rain expected to cause rivers to flash flood.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood-alert actions include preparing the flood plan and readying insurance documents and medicines.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood-warning actions include moving people, pets and valuables to safety and following emergency-service instructions.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Official advice says to turn off gas, electricity and water if it is safe during a flood warning.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Official advice says not to walk, cycle or drive through flood water.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood alerts can indicate risk to fields, recreational land, car parks, minor roads, farmland and exposed coasts.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood warnings can indicate risk to homes, businesses, railways, roads, campsites and major attractions.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood-warning signup
rows.verified: Environment Agency flood-warning registration is free for homes and organisations in England where the service is available.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood-warning signup
rows.verified: Registered users can receive flood warnings by telephone call, text message or email.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood-warning signup
rows.verified: Depending on location, messages can cover flooding from rivers, the sea or groundwater.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood alerts are usually issued about 2 to 12 hours before flooding, so the timing is typical rather than guaranteed.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood alerts and warnings
rows.verified: Flood warnings are usually issued about 30 minutes to 2 hours before flooding, so lead time can vary.

rows.source: Environment Agency flood-warning signup
rows.verified: The warning-registration service does not provide surface-water or flash-flood warnings, so another current source is required for that hazard.
